intro: Look after customers once they have bought: tickets for the problems they raise, conversations with customers and suppliers, and the visits and calls you book with them. You can see who has each one and how long it has waited.
start: Open your first ticket for a customer problem, so the team can see who has it.
Answer the conversations that are assigned to you, then the unassigned ones.
Book your next customer visit or call in Appointments.

articles.title: Answer a customer's ticket
articles.summary: Take the ticket, reply to the customer or leave a note only your team sees, then resolve it and ask how it went.

steps.rest: for a new problem. Choose the customer, give the subject and what happened, set the priority and kind, and press Open ticket.

steps.rest: write it, and press Send reply or Add note. The customer sees replies; notes are only for your team.

tips: Each ticket shows when its first reply is due, set by its priority. Oldest unanswered first puts the longest waiting at the top.
Tickets that name an invoice or a waybill keep the link, so the next person sees what it is about.
If a critical ticket has nobody on it for a while, the people who manage tickets are told.

articles.title: Book a visit or call with a customer
articles.summary: Book appointments by the week, mark how each went, and accept or turn down the times customers ask for.

steps.rest: Choose the customer, say what it is, when it starts and how long it is, and press Book it.
